en: Jose Rizal published his second novel, El Filibusterismo, in Ghent, Belgium, in the year 1891.
Emilio Aguinaldo proclaimed Philippine independence from Spain on June 12, 1898, in Kawit, Cavite.
The Supreme Court of the Philippines is composed of one Chief Justice and fourteen Associate Justices.
Filipino citizens who are at least eighteen years old and registered can vote in national elections.
The Philippine eagle, also known as the monkey-eating eagle, is the national bird of the Philippines.
The Sinulog festival in Cebu honors the Santo Niño with a traditional two-step forward, one-step backward dance.
The Ifugao people of the Cordillera region carved the famous Banaue Rice Terraces into the mountains.
Baybayin is an ancient pre-colonial Philippine writing system that uses specific characters to represent spoken syllables.
The Filipino value of bayanihan refers to the tradition of neighbors helping a family move their house.
Dr. Fe del Mundo invented a bamboo incubator to provide affordable healthcare for premature babies in rural areas.
Guillermo Tolentino sculpted the Bonifacio Monument in Caloocan and the Oblation statue at the University of the Philippines.
The Puerto Princesa Subterranean River in Palawan features a navigable underground river that flows directly into the sea.
